messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need a crisp launch gate for the Optimize toolkit pilot that ties eval-triggered alerts to quantization fallback behavior. Customer asks from RetailX and FinNova are pushing this into scope. Thoughts?
liam: +1 on gating. do we want a single golden-metric or a tiered gate? latency spikes vs quality regressions differ.
jordan: Tiered makes sense. propose: P0 = severe quality regression (auto rollback), P1 = sustained latency > SLA, P2 = degraded perf but within SLO.
maya: Agree. Also need to decide who owns automated rollback vs operator notification. RetailX requires automatic fallback to FP16 if int8 causes >2% rouge drop.
sarah: That 2% threshold is tight — do we have reliable eval sets for RetailX flows? We might need per-customer eval hooks.
liam: We can wire eval-triggered alerts to per-route prompt sets. optimize-bot can run nightly evals and surface deltas.
optimize-bot: nightly-eval job completed: models/redwood-ggml-v2 int8 -> RougeDelta: 1.3% (baseline fp16).
jordan: For pilot gate, let's require: 1) per-route eval jobs configured, 2) automatic fallback policy present, 3) canary traffic rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with manual hold step, 4) observable alerting thresholds documented.
maya: Drafting launch criteria now. Quick checklist: ```- per-route evalset configured (yes/no) - fallback policy implemented (yes/no) - canary rollout plan in infra (yes/no) - SLOs documented and verified (latency P95, quality metric) - post-rollout eval job scheduled (daily)```
sarah: We should add a customer acceptance item: RetailX must sign off on fallback behavior for their top 10 prompt templates.
liam: Ops concern: fallback to FP16 increases cost by ~18% for some models. Need to add econ acceptance (cost delta < X% or exec signoff).
maya: Good catch. Add: "cost delta explained + product signoff" to the checklist.
jordan: On alerts: propose two alert flavors — immediate high-severity alert that triggers rollback, and a low-severity trend alert for SRE/product. Example: ```- high: quality delta > 2% over 1 hour -> auto-rollover/fallback - low: quality delta 0.5%-2% over 24h -> notify product & SRE```
sarah: And include deterministic reproducibility step: when an alert fires, we must run a focused eval minimizing randomness (fixed seed, 3-run median). Put that in runbook.
maya: Who will own the runbook? @liam / ops?
liam: Ops will own the runbook but Product (maya) owns customer signoff criteria.
optimize-bot: canary-rollout job created: tag=v0.1-optimize-canary, pipeline=https://ci.internal/runs/789
maya: Next actions: liam to draft runbook + fallback implementation plan (due EOD Wed), jordan to draft per-route eval spec and sample evalset (due Fri), sarah to confirm RetailX test templates and signoff flow. I'll consolidate checklist and send for review.
liam: Ack. planning a short playbook PR with shell commands for rollback and metrics to watch, e.g.: ```bash
# check eval delta
python infra/eval/compare.py --route retailx-cart --baseline fp16 --variant int8
# trigger fallback
redwoodctl rollout fallback --route retailx-cart --target fp16
```
jordan: Also recommend adding a soft-fail mode where we keep quantization but reduce max tokens to cap latency while preserving lower cost — could be a middle ground before full fallback.
maya: Nice idea, add to options column in playbook.
sarah: RetailX onboarding call scheduled Thu 10am — I'll get their top 10 prompts before then.
maya: Thanks everyone — I'll post the consolidated checklist + preliminary runbook after the RetailX call. :thumbsup:
